appfunction.description:
Searches for images and videos based on a user's text query. This function is designed to parse the user's request for specific details like dates, time ranges, and locations (city and country) to perform a refined search. For optimal results, you should extract these details into the corresponding optional fields (startTime, endTime, city, country, countryCode) whenever they are mentioned, in addition to creating a detailed queryString.
**IMPORTANT:** The findPhotos tool returns machine-level URIs (content://...) intended exclusively for the backend UI widget. When processing these results, you must extract only the total count of the items found.
Limit your text output to a natural, friendly conversational summary. Acknowledge that you searched Samsung Gallery and state the number of items found. Ensure your final response consists entirely of standard natural language words and numbers.
**KEYWORD SEARCH LIMITATION — Actions/Verbs Not Supported in keyword:** The keyword field does NOT support action-based or verb-based values. Action or activity terms (e.g., cutting, drinking, eating, holding, reading, riding, dancing, kissing, running, sitting, playing, driving, swimming, cooking, jumping, sleeping, walking, etc.) will NOT return relevant results when used as a keyword. When the user's request involves an action, omit the action from the keyword and extract only the subject/object/entity involved. If the request consists solely of an action with no identifiable subject or object, set keyword to null and inform the user that action-based searches are not currently supported in Samsung Gallery.

parameters.name: queryString
parameters.description: (Required) Contains only the part of the user's utterance or input relevant to photo search. This should contain only the descriptive part of the user's request that relates to the photos or videos being searched for, including modifiers like location, time, subjects, and other qualifying attributes. Command words like "find", "show", "get" should be excluded, keeping only the content description. Examples: - "photos I took in Paris last year" (from "Find photos I took in Paris last year") - "pictures from my trip to Tokyo in December" (from "Show me pictures from my trip to Tokyo in December") - "videos of my dog playing in the park yesterday" (from "Videos of my dog playing in the park yesterday") - "sunset photos from my vacation in Hawaii" (from "Find sunset photos from my vacation in Hawaii")

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: (Optional) A normalized keyword string extracted from the user's request to support retrieval. This should contain the most salient search terms mentioned by the user (and may include multiple tokens if needed), such as a subject/entity/object (e.g., "dog"), clothing or accessories, or a distinctive attribute. **Do NOT include action verbs or activities** (e.g., running, eating, dancing, holding, driving, playing, sitting, reading, riding, kissing, etc.) as the search engine cannot match actions. Instead, extract only the noun-based subjects or objects from the user's request. Command words like "find", "show", "get" should be excluded. If the user mentions time or location, those should be populated in their dedicated fields (startTime/endTime/city/country/countryCode) rather than relying on this keyword. Although optional, it should be populated whenever a meaningful keyword can be extracted. Use null only when no suitable keyword exists. If the user's request contains only time and/or location without any additional subject/entity/object/attribute, set keyword to null. If the user's request contains only an action with no identifiable subject or object, set keyword to null. Examples: - "glasses" (from "Find photos of me wearing glasses from last week") - "plane" (from "Show me pictures I took on a plane in February") - "red outfit" (from "Find photos of me wearing a red outfit") - "son microphone" (from "Find photos of my son holding a microphone" — action "holding" omitted, nouns kept) - "dad" (from "Show me photos of dad driving in July" — action "driving" omitted, subject kept) - null (from "Find photos I took in Paris in 2023") - null (from "Show me photos of people dancing" — only action, no distinct subject/object)

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: (Optional) The start time of the search range (it SHOULD be local time). Although optional, must be populated when the user mentions specific dates, time periods, or relative time references.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: (Optional) The end time of the search range (it SHOULD be local time). Similar to [startTime], although optional, must be populated when a time range is explicitly mentioned.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: (Optional) The name of the city, expressed in the input language. Although optional, must be populated when the user mentions a specific city or urban location.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: (Optional) The name of the country, expressed in the input language. Although optional, must be populated when the user mentions a specific country.

parameters.name: countryCode
parameters.description: (Optional) The ISO country code for the mentioned location (e.g., "KR", "US", "AU"). Although optional, must be populated when a country is mentioned or can be inferred from a city name. Must be uppercase.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: (Optional) The content type to search for. Supported values: - "Image" — Search only images - "Video" — Search only videos Although optional, must be populated when the user explicitly requests only videos or only images/photos; if not specified, search both.

parameters.name: orderType
parameters.description: (Optional) To determines the order in which the content is listed ("latest" or "oldest") Supported values: - "latest" — Most recent first - "oldest" — Earliest first

parameters.name: maxCount
parameters.description: (Optional) The maximum number of results requested.

response.description: FindPhotosResponse The found content's response with media items and resources (MAX = 50)

The title of the album.
The parameters for finding albums. A null value means that there is no restriction on the given field. If all fields are null, it returns all the albums (up to [maxCount]).

The query to search for albums. A null value means to query all albums.
This parameter is analogous to the caller typing a query into a search box. The app providing the app function has full control over how the query is interpreted and processed; for example by name matching or semantic analysis.
The maximum number of albums to return.
The parameters for finding media items. A null value means that there is no restriction on the given field. If all fields are null, it returns all the media items (up to [maxCount]).

The [DateTime] on or after which a media item must have been modified to be included in the results.
Acts as a lower bound for filtering media items based on their modification item. A `null` value means no lower bound is applied.
If [startTime] is equal to [endTime], an empty list will be returned.
[androidx.appfunctions.AppFunctionInvalidArgumentException] should be thrown if [startTime] is specified and is after [endTime].

The [DateTime] before which a media item must have been modified to be included in the results.
Acts as a strict upper bound for filtering media items based on their modification itemstamp. A `null` value means no upper bound is applied.
If [startTime] is equal to [endTime], an empty list will be returned.
[androidx.appfunctions.AppFunctionInvalidArgumentException] should be thrown if [startTime] is specified and is after [endTime].

The search query to be processed. A null value means to query all media items with the remaining parameters.
This parameter is analogous to the caller typing a query into a search box. The app providing the app function has full control over how the query is interpreted and processed; for example by name matching or semantic analysis.

An interface for [@Document] classes that carry a decision to set a field of the given type in an entity. These `Set*Field` classes are used as properties of `Upgrade*Params` classes, always nullable. The convention is that when the property is set to `null`, the field of the entity is not modified. Otherwise, it is set to the value carried by the `Set*Field` object. In particular, for a nullable field, that value could be `null` which allows setting a field of the entity to `null`.
